function.name: game_functions_solve_jigsaw
function.description: Generate solution for a given jigsaw puzzle image. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

puzzle_image.description: The image file of the jigsaw puzzle.

pieces_count.description: Number of pieces in the jigsaw puzzle.

solve_method.description: Method to be used to solve the puzzle. Default is brute_force.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have a built‑in “create” capability – my toolbox only lets me **solve** existing jigsaw images (via the `game_functions_solve_jigsaw` API). If you’d like to make your own puzzle, here’s what you could do:

| Step | What to Do | Suggested Tool / Resource |
|------|------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | Pick a photo or graphic you want turned into a puzzle. | Any digital image editor (Photoshop, GIMP, Paint.NET) |
| 2 | Decide on piece count & shape. | Online generators like *Jigsaw Puzzle Maker* (https://www.jigsawplanet.com/), *PuzzleMaker*, or *Piczzle*. They let you choose standard shapes (e.g., interlocking tabs) and set the number of pieces. |
| 3 | Upload the image to the generator. | Most sites accept JPEG/PNG up to ~10 MB. |
| 4 | Configure settings: edge style, piece size, optional border, background color, etc. | Use the UI sliders/options on the site. |
| 5 | Export/download the finished puzzle. | Usually gives you a printable PDF or PNG grid ready for cutting. |

If you prefer doing it manually:
1. Import the image into an editing program.
2. Overlay a grid matching your desired piece count.
3. Convert each cell into a separate layer/piece.
4. Add interlocking edges via vector paths or clip masks.
5. Save/export each piece individually.

Once you’ve created the puzzle image(s), feel free to share one with me—then I can attempt to solve it using the `game_functions_solve_jigsaw` tool!
